3. INSTALLING AND STARTING
==========================

Unpack the archive where you want the game, for example with LhA:
    lha x xenon-1.5-aros-x86_64.lha Work:
or open it with Unarc or another archiver. This creates the drawer
"Xenon" with the program, its icon and this ReadMe.

The game's data
  The archive does not contain the game itself. Its pictures, music and
  scripts belong to the original release (C's Ware, 1994) and go into one
  data file, xenon.pak, which you make from your own copy of the PC-98
  game: the five floppy disks or an installed hard disk, as disk images
  (D88, HDI, NHD, ...) or as plain files. On a computer with Python 3, in
  the source distribution:
      make data SRC=<your copy of the game>
      make pack
  (docs/game-data.md there explains it). It checks every file against
  the original release before using it. A xenon.pak someone else made
  for this version of the game works the same way. Put xenon.pak into
  the drawer "Xenon", next to the program (or give its place with PAK=,
  section 5).

From Wanderer: open the drawer and double-click the XENON icon.
From the Shell:
    cd Work:Xenon
    xenon
Options go on the command line, for example "xenon LANG=ja". Quote a value
that contains "=" or spaces. "version xenon" in the Shell shows which
version you have. From Wanderer the options are tool types of the icon
(section 5).

Saved games go to the drawer "saves/xenon" inside the game's drawer. The
game creates it on first use. If the game's drawer is write-protected, saves go
to ENVARC:xenon/xenon instead. If neither works, they go to T: and are lost when
you switch the machine off. Saves are the same files as in the AmigaOS
version and can be copied between the two.

Save files of the PC-98 version cannot be loaded.

Coming from version 1.4 or older
  Older versions kept the saves directly in the drawer "saves" (or in
  ENVARC:Xenon) as save1.dat ... save4.dat and progress.dat. Move them
  into "saves/xenon" and drop the ".dat": save1 ... save4, progress.
  The tool types MUSICVOL and VOICEVOL are now VOLUME and VOICEVOLUME.
  On a PC keyboard F1 is Help now, no longer F11.

Keys on a PC keyboard
  F1 does the work of the Amiga's Help key (section 4). The left Windows
  key is the Left Amiga key, so Left Amiga+N and Left Amiga+M below are
  the left Windows key with N or M.

Voices (optional)
  The Windows 95 version of Xenon (1997) has the characters speak most of
  their lines. This game can play those voices with its text, in every
  language (the voices are Japanese). They are not in this archive: the
  voice data file xenon_voice.pak is made from your own copy of the
  Windows version (its file XENON.DAT) with the tools of the source
  distribution (make voice-pack, described in docs/voice.md there). Put
  xenon_voice.pak in the game's drawer, next to xenon.pak; the game finds
  it at start-up (or give VOICEPAK=, section 5). NOVOICE turns the voices
  off again.
  Either kind of voice data works: the Opus one (make voice-pack, 48 MB)
  or the original one (CODEC=ldp6, 261 MB). The voices play as a second
  AHI channel, so the AHI unit needs at least two channels in the AHI
  preferences (the default is four); with one, use VOICEMIX. AHI mixes
  everything at the unit's frequency: 44.1 or 48 kHz keeps the voices'
  full quality.
